2027-04-02.title: Friday of All the Confessors (Sakala Mawdyanmar) · Friday of Hevoro week
readings: Of whom the world was not worthy
Everyone who acknowledges me before others, I also will acknowledge
2027-04-02.alt: Hevoro week, the first week of the season of Qyomtho (the Resurrection). Hevoro means white: the week is kept as one great day of Easter joy, and it closes with New Sunday. The Panchangam names this Friday after the Resurrection the day of All the Confessors (സകല മൗദ്യാനന്മാർ).
2027-04-02.verse: Everyone therefore who acknowledges me before others, I also will acknowledge before my Father in heaven.
theo: Christ is risen! On the first Friday after Qyomtho the Church does not return to the Friday of the Cross alone; she keeps the memory of all the confessors. In the Syriac tradition a mawdyono, a confessor, is one who confessed Christ openly before others and bore the cost: prison, exile, torture, and for many, death. The Panchangam calls this day the Friday of All the Confessors (Sakala Mawdyanmar). It is fitting that they are remembered in the white week. On Good Friday the Lord went down into death; on this Friday we honor those who followed him there and now share his victory. The Book of Revelation sees them “robed in white” before the throne, having “washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.” Hevoro, the white week of the newly baptized, is also the week of the white robes of the witnesses. The Letter to the Hebrews names some of the heroes of faith of the old covenant and then lists those whose names it does not give: “Others suffered mocking and flogging, and even chains and imprisonment. They were stoned to death, they were sawn in two, they were killed by the sword.” Then comes a sentence that every age of persecution has repeated with gratitude: they were people “of whom the world was not worthy.”

Why did they not deny Christ? Today's Gospel gives the Lord's own reasons. First, nothing stays hidden: “What I say to you in the dark, tell in the light; and what you hear whispered, proclaim from the housetops.” Second, the worst that persecutors can do has a limit: “Do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul.” Third, we are known and loved in every detail: “Are not two sparrows sold for a penny? Yet not one of them will fall to the ground apart from your Father. And even the hairs of your head are all counted. So do not be afraid; you are of more value than many sparrows.” And finally, a promise: “Everyone therefore who acknowledges me before others, I also will acknowledge before my Father in heaven.” Tertullian told the rulers of his time that the blood of Christians is seed: the more they were mown down, the more they grew (in substance). Hebrews ends with a mystery: those heroes “did not receive what was promised, since God had provided something better so that they would not, apart from us, be made perfect.” The confessors of every age wait to be made perfect together with us, in the one Body of the risen Christ.

How do we keep the Friday of All the Confessors? Remember the confessors of our own land: St Thomas the Apostle, who according to the tradition of our Churches gave his life for Christ in India; and the Christians of our own time in India and elsewhere who have lost homes, health or life rather than deny the Lord. Pray today for all who suffer for the faith, and if you can, give to a fund that helps persecuted Christians. Ask the Virgin Mary, whom the Church invokes as Queen of Confessors, for courage. Then look at your own day: where am I silent about Christ out of fear of laughter or of losing favor? A word at the office, a sign of the cross before a meal in a restaurant, a Sunday kept holy against pressure: these are small confessions, and the Lord who counts the hairs of our head does not forget them. Come to the Holy Qurbono, where the risen Lord whom the confessors acknowledged gives himself to us.
outline: Ask: when did I last speak of Christ when it would have been easier to stay silent?
Point 1 · Of whom the world was not worthy
The heroes of Hebrews 11 and the confessors of every age.
The sparrows and the hairs of our head.
Small confessions and a great promise.
“Everyone therefore who acknowledges me before others, I also will acknowledge before my Father in heaven.”
live: Pray today by name for a country or a community where Christians suffer for their faith; give something, if you can, to help them.
Today, in a place where it costs you a little, make the sign of the cross or say a word about Christ without shame.
2027-04-02.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, risen and glorious, you promised to acknowledge before your Father everyone who acknowledges you before others. We thank you for all the confessors who held fast to you in chains, in exile and in death, of whom the world was not worthy. Through their prayers strengthen the Christians who suffer for your name today. Deliver us from the fear that keeps us silent, and teach us that we are of more value than many sparrows. With the Virgin Mary, Queen of Confessors, and all your witnesses, we praise you with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: The confessors drew their strength from the Body and Blood of the Lord; in the Holy Qurbono the same risen Christ strengthens us to confess him before others.

quick: This Friday after the Resurrection the Church remembers all the confessors, who confessed Christ at the cost of suffering or death.
Hebrews calls the heroes of faith people “of whom the world was not worthy.”
Jesus promises to acknowledge before the Father everyone who acknowledges him before others.
2027-04-02.action: Pray by name for one community where Christians are persecuted today.
2027-04-02.question: Where does fear keep me silent about Christ?

family.explain: Jesus told his friends not to be afraid. God takes care of even a little sparrow, and he knows how many hairs are on our heads. Many Christians, long ago and today, have been brave and said “I belong to Jesus,” even when people were cruel to them. Today the Church remembers all of them. Jesus says that when we speak up for him, he will speak up for us before his Father.
family.intention: We pray for Christians who are being hurt or treated badly because they love Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “Where can each of us be brave for Jesus this week?”

illus: A young engineer from Kollam joined a firm abroad where his team leader liked to make jokes about religion at lunch. For months he laughed along and said nothing. In Hevoro week he read, in a small book of saints his mother had packed, about the Christians of the early centuries who were offered release if they would only say one word against Christ. The next day, when the jokes began, he said quietly, “I am a Christian, and I would rather you did not laugh at the things I love.” There was a silence. Later, a colleague from another country stopped him in the corridor and said that she was a Catholic too, and had never dared to say so.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, on this Friday of All the Confessors we thank you for all who acknowledged you before others. Give us their courage. Amen.
share: Of whom the world was not worthy (Hebrews 11:38). Which witness of the faith has touched my life most?
So do not be afraid; you are of more value than many sparrows (Matthew 10:31). What fear do I bring to the Lord tonight?
Everyone therefore who acknowledges me before others, I also will acknowledge before my Father in heaven (Matthew 10:32). Where is the Lord asking me to acknowledge him?
pm.resp: Risen Lord, make us faithful confessors of your name.
interc: For the Church in every land where Christians are persecuted, that they may be strong and that their persecutors may come to know Christ.
For Christians in India who suffer for their faith, and for peace and justice in our country.
For those who are tempted to deny the faith out of fear, that the Lord may hold them fast.
For all who have died for Christ, that they may rejoice in the white robes of the Lamb.
For ourselves, that we may confess Christ with gentleness and courage in our homes and workplaces.
pm.close: Father, in every age you have raised up confessors who bore witness to your Son with their lives. Let their example and their prayers make us faithful, deliver us from fear, and bring us with them to the glory of the Resurrection. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! On this first Friday after Qyomtho our Church remembers all the confessors: those who confessed Christ before others and paid for it with prison, exile or death. The Letter to the Hebrews calls them people of whom the world was not worthy (Hebrews 11:38).

Why did they stand firm? The Lord tells us in the Gospel. Do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Not a sparrow falls without your Father; even the hairs of your head are counted. So do not be afraid; you are of more value than many sparrows (Matthew 10:31).

And he gives a promise: Everyone who acknowledges me before others, I also will acknowledge before my Father in heaven (Matthew 10:32). In this white week we see the confessors, with Revelation, robed in white, their robes washed in the blood of the Lamb.

Let us pray today for Christians who suffer for the faith, ask the Virgin Mary, Queen of Confessors, for courage, and make our own small confessions: a sign of the cross, a word for Christ, a Sunday kept holy. The risen Lord does not forget them. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Today we remember all the brave Christians who said “I belong to Jesus,” even when people hurt them for it. Jesus said: do not be afraid! God looks after every little sparrow, and he even knows how many hairs are on your head. Can you be brave for Jesus today, maybe by making the sign of the cross before you eat?

intro: Theme: “Everyone therefore who acknowledges me before others, I also will acknowledge before my Father in heaven.”
On the Friday of All the Confessors: the witnesses of whom the world was not worthy, the Lord's word against fear, and his promise to all who confess him.

points.h: Of whom the world was not worthy
sub: The named and the unnamed heroes of faith.
Robes made white in the blood of the Lamb.
q: If our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the furnace of blazing fire and out of your hand, O king, let him deliver us.
These are they who have come out of the great ordeal; they have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.
points.apply: Pray today by name for Christians who suffer for the faith, and help them if you can.

sub: Two sparrows and the hairs of your head.
q: Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name, you are mine.
There is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear;
points.apply: Name one fear that keeps you silent about Christ, and hand it over to him in prayer.

sub: The Lord acknowledges his own before the Father.
q: Precious in the sight of the LORD is the death of his faithful ones.
because if you confess with your lips that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.
points.apply: Make one small, gentle confession of Christ today in a place where it costs you something.

concl: The confessors share the Lord's death and now his victory; in the white week we see them robed in white.
The risen Lord who counts the hairs of our head will acknowledge before his Father all who acknowledge him.
2027-04-02.resolve: Confess Christ gently and without fear: pray for the persecuted, ask the Virgin Mary, Queen of Confessors, for courage, and receive strength at the Holy Qurbono.
